items.title: UK and Finland condemn Israeli killing of journalist in Lebanon as 'intolerable'

featured_image.name: Amal Khalil: Israel Accused of War Crimes After Journalist Death

items.description: The United Kingdom and Finland on Saturday jointly condemned Israeli attacks on journalists in Lebanon, calling the violence "intolerable" in a statement issued in their capacity as co-chairs of the Media Freedom Coalition. The declaration came three days after Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed in an Israeli airstrike on the southern Lebanese village of al-Tiri on April 22.[1][2]

items.title: Traders warn Hormuz oil shock will force harsh demand crash

featured_image.name: Oil rises after Iran, US attack ships as tensions escalate over Hormuz

items.description: The Strait of Hormuz crisis, now approaching its second month, has thrust the United States into the role of emergency supplier to the world while top energy traders warn that the worst of the demand shock is still ahead. With the vital waterway largely closed since late February and diplomatic efforts stalled, global oil markets face a collision between record American exports and an accelerating collapse in consumption.

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi on Saturday laid out Tehran's demands and rejected what it called "maximalist" U.S. positions during talks in Islamabad, as Pakistan pushed to revive diplomacy and end a war that has killed thousands and disrupted global energy markets.[1][2]

items.title: Trump cancels Witkoff-Kushner trip to Pakistan for Iran talks

featured_image.name: Trump to send envoys to Islamabad as Iran rules out direct talks

items.description:
President Donald Trump abruptly canceled a planned trip by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan for peace talks with Iran on Saturday, Fox News reported, just one day after the White House had confirmed the two would travel to Islamabad for a second round of ceasefire negotiations.[1][2][3]

The cancellation came after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi left Islamabad on Saturday evening without meeting any American representatives, according to two Pakistani officials who spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity. Araghchi had met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir during his brief stay, but his government had made clear from the outset that no direct talks with U.S. officials were planned.[4][5][6]

items.title: Palestinians vote in first Gaza election in 20 years

featured_image.name: Gaza area votes in first municipal election in 20 years

items.description:
Palestinians across the occupied West Bank and in the central Gaza city of Deir al-Balah cast ballots on Saturday in municipal elections, marking the first vote in Gaza in two decades and the first electoral event in either territory since the start of the Israel-Hamas war in October 2023.

Polling stations opened at 7 a.m. local time, with nearly 1.5 million people registered to vote in the West Bank and approximately 70,000 eligible in Deir al-Balah, according to the Ramallah-based Central Elections Commission. Polls in the West Bank were set to close at 7 p.m., while those in Deir al-Balah were scheduled to shut at 5 p.m. to allow for counting in daylight, given the lack of electricity in the war-ravaged territory.[1][2][3]

items.title: U.S. envoys head to Pakistan as Iran refuses direct talks

featured_image.name: White House confirms Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner Pakistan trip for Iran  talks

items.description:
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are headed to Islamabad on Saturday for what the White House has called a second round of peace talks with Iran, even as Tehran insists it will not engage in direct negotiations with American officials.[1][2][3]

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in the Pakistani capital on Friday evening and on Saturday met with Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. But Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei said Araghchi's discussions would be limited to "high-ranking Pakistani officials," with Iran's positions conveyed to the U.S. side through Pakistani mediators.[4][2][5][6][7]

items.description: Nearly two months after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz plunged global energy markets into turmoil, the world's largest oil traders are warning that the worst is yet to come — not from the supply side, but from the demand destruction that is now spreading beyond Asia and into the broader global economy.

items.title: U.S. Navy begins clearing Iranian mines from Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: US says it's clearing Iranian mines in effort to open the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: The U.S. Navy is working to clear Iranian mines from the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply typically passes, even as a fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran shows signs of strain and diplomatic efforts to end the weekslong war remain uncertain.[1][2]

items.title: IEA chief says oil crisis has permanently broken fossil fuel industry

featured_image.name: IEA approves third term for chief Fatih Birol pushing clean energy,  ETEnergyworld

items.description:
The oil crisis triggered by the war in Iran has irreversibly changed the global fossil fuel industry, turning countries away from oil and gas toward cleaner alternatives, International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said this week.

"The vase is broken, the damage is done — it will be very difficult to put the pieces back together. This will have permanent consequences for the global energy markets for years to come," Birol told The Guardian in remarks reported on Thursday.[1][2]
